topicName: The National Economy and Economic Development
description: This topic examines Tanzania's national economy, its sectors and main economic activities, the role of government and financial institutions, sources of revenue and the national budget, investment and entrepreneurship, and economic problems and their solutions.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by the term 'national economy'?

options.text: The total system of producing, distributing and using goods and services in a country
The amount of money kept in the Bank of Tanzania
The salaries paid to government workers only
The buying and selling done in a single market

mcq.explanation: The national economy is the whole system through which a country produces, distributes and consumes goods and services to meet people's needs.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following activities belongs to the primary sector of the economy?

options.text: Manufacturing soap in a factory
Growing maize and harvesting it
Teaching in a secondary school
Selling clothes in a shop

mcq.explanation: The primary sector involves extracting raw materials directly from nature, such as farming, mining, fishing and forestry.

mcq.questionText: Turning raw cotton into finished cloth in a factory is an example of which sector?

options.text: Primary sector
Tertiary sector
Secondary sector
Informal sector

mcq.explanation: The secondary sector processes or manufactures raw materials into finished goods, for example turning cotton into cloth.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a service in the tertiary sector?

options.text: Mining gold at Geita
Banking services offered by CRDB Bank
Catching fish in Lake Victoria
Making cement in a factory

mcq.explanation: The tertiary sector provides services rather than goods, such as banking, transport, tourism, education and health.

mcq.questionText: Which economic activity employs the largest number of people in Tanzania?

options.text: Tourism
Mining
Agriculture
Banking

mcq.explanation: Agriculture is the backbone of Tanzania's economy and employs the majority of the population, especially in rural areas.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major mineral mined in Tanzania?

options.text: Gold
Crude oil
Uranium ore exported as cars
Silk

mcq.explanation: Gold is one of Tanzania's leading minerals, mined in areas such as Geita, Kahama and Bulyanhulu, and is a major source of foreign exchange.

mcq.questionText: What is the main role of the Bank of Tanzania (BOT)?

options.text: To give loans directly to all citizens for farming
To act as the central bank that issues currency and controls monetary policy
To collect taxes from businesses
To build roads and bridges

mcq.explanation: The Bank of Tanzania is the central bank; it issues the national currency (the shilling), controls the money supply and supervises other banks.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax?

options.text: Value Added Tax (VAT) on goods
Import duty on imported items
Income tax paid by an employed person
Excise duty on soft drinks

mcq.explanation: A direct tax is paid directly from a person's or company's income or profit, such as income tax and corporate tax. VAT and duties are indirect taxes.

mcq.questionText: Which government institution is responsible for collecting taxes in Tanzania?

options.text: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
Bank of Tanzania (BOT)
National Examinations Council (NECTA)
Tanzania Ports Authority (TPA)

mcq.explanation: The Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) is the body charged with assessing and collecting government taxes and duties.

options.text: A list of all banks operating in the country
A government plan of expected revenue and planned expenditure for a financial year
The total savings of all citizens
The amount of foreign aid received in a year

mcq.explanation: The national budget is the government's financial plan showing how much money it expects to collect and how it intends to spend it during a financial year.

options.text: A fall in the prices of all goods
A general and continuous rise in the prices of goods and services
An increase in the number of banks
A rise in the value of the shilling

mcq.explanation: Inflation is a persistent general increase in prices, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

options.text: A government ministry for trade
A savings and credit cooperative society where members save and borrow
A type of foreign loan
A central bank branch

mcq.explanation: A SACCOS (Savings and Credit Cooperative Society) is a member-owned financial institution where people save together and obtain affordable loans.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes entrepreneurship?

options.text: Working for a salary in a government office
Starting and running a business while taking risks to make profit
Saving money in a commercial bank
Paying taxes to the government

mcq.explanation: Entrepreneurship is the ability to identify opportunities and start a business, organising resources and taking risks in order to earn profit.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of foreign investment in Tanzania?

options.text: A Tanzanian farmer opening a small shop in his village
A SACCOS giving loans to local members
A company from another country building a mine or factory in Tanzania
Citizens paying income tax to TRA

mcq.explanation: Foreign investment occurs when individuals or companies from other countries invest capital in Tanzania, for example in mining, manufacturing or tourism.

mcq.questionText: Why is it important for citizens to pay their taxes?

options.text: Because taxes are kept privately by tax officers
Because tax revenue funds public services like schools, hospitals and roads
Because paying tax increases inflation
Because it reduces the value of the shilling

mcq.explanation: Taxes are the main source of government revenue used to provide public services and infrastructure that benefit all citizens.

fib.questionText: The sector of the economy that extracts raw materials directly from nature, such as farming and mining, is called the _____ sector.
fib.explanation: The primary sector deals with the direct extraction of natural resources, including agriculture, mining, fishing and forestry.

fib.questionText: The processing of raw materials into finished goods in factories belongs to the _____ sector.
fib.explanation: The secondary sector manufactures and processes raw materials into usable products.

fib.questionText: The central bank of Tanzania, which issues the national currency, is the Bank of _____.
fib.explanation: The Bank of Tanzania (BOT) is the central bank responsible for issuing currency and controlling monetary policy.

fib.questionText: A tax that is paid directly from a person's income or a company's profit is called a _____ tax.
fib.explanation: Direct taxes, such as income tax, are paid directly to the government from earnings or profits.

fib.questionText: Value Added Tax (VAT) charged on goods and services is an example of an _____ tax.
fib.explanation: Indirect taxes are added to the price of goods and services and paid by the consumer when buying them.

fib.questionText: The government body responsible for collecting taxes in Tanzania is the Tanzania Revenue _____.
fib.explanation: The Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) assesses and collects taxes on behalf of the government.

fib.questionText: A continuous general rise in the prices of goods and services is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money because the same amount buys fewer goods.

fib.questionText: A member-owned society where people save together and borrow at low interest is abbreviated as _____.
fib.explanation: SACCOS stands for Savings and Credit Cooperative Society and helps members access affordable credit.

fib.questionText: The government's annual plan showing expected revenue and planned expenditure is called the national _____.
fib.explanation: The national budget guides how the government collects and spends money during the financial year.

fib.questionText: A situation where people who are able and willing to work cannot find jobs is called _____.
fib.explanation: Unemployment is a serious economic problem that reduces income and can increase poverty and crime.

tf.questionText: Tourism, banking and transport all belong to the tertiary (service) sector of the economy.
tf.explanation: The tertiary sector provides services rather than goods, including tourism, banking and transport.

tf.questionText: Agriculture employs only a small minority of Tanzanians.
tf.explanation: Agriculture is the backbone of the economy and employs the majority of Tanzanians, especially in rural areas.

tf.questionText: The Bank of Tanzania is responsible for issuing the country's currency.
tf.explanation: As the central bank, the Bank of Tanzania has the sole authority to issue the national currency, the shilling.

tf.questionText: Income tax is an example of an indirect tax.
tf.explanation: Income tax is a direct tax because it is paid directly from a person's earnings. VAT and customs duties are indirect taxes.

tf.questionText: Loans and grants from foreign countries and organisations are sources of government revenue.
tf.explanation: Besides taxes and fees, the government also obtains revenue from loans and grants (aid) from other countries and international institutions.

tf.questionText: Inflation increases the purchasing power of money.
tf.explanation: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money because prices rise and the same amount buys fewer goods.

tf.questionText: Investment helps to create jobs and promote economic development.
tf.explanation: Investment in businesses and projects creates employment, increases production and contributes to national development.

tf.questionText: Excessive foreign borrowing can lead to a heavy national debt burden.
tf.explanation: When a country borrows too much from abroad, repaying the debt and its interest can strain the economy and limit development spending.

tf.questionText: Commercial banks such as NMB and CRDB exist mainly to print the national currency.
tf.explanation: Commercial banks accept deposits, give loans and offer financial services; only the central bank (BOT) issues currency.

tf.questionText: Depending too much on a few export crops or imported goods can make an economy vulnerable.
tf.explanation: Economic dependency on a few products or on imports makes a country vulnerable to price changes and external shocks.

summary.questionText: Name the three main sectors of the economy.
summary.explanation: Economic activities are grouped into the primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing) and tertiary (services) sectors.

summary.questionText: List four main economic activities carried out in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Agriculture, mining, tourism and fishing (also industry and trade).
summary.explanation: Tanzania's economy is driven by activities such as agriculture, mining, tourism, fishing, industry and trade.

summary.questionText: State two sources of government revenue.
summary.correctAnswer: Taxes (direct and indirect) and fees; also loans and grants.
summary.explanation: The government raises money mainly through taxes and fees, and supplements this with loans and grants from external sources.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between a direct tax and an indirect tax.
summary.correctAnswer: A direct tax is paid directly from income or profit (e.g. income tax), while an indirect tax is added to the price of goods and services (e.g. VAT).
summary.explanation: Direct taxes fall on earnings, while indirect taxes are paid when buying goods and services.

summary.questionText: Mention three functions of the Bank of Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Issuing currency, controlling the money supply, and supervising other banks (banker to the government).
summary.explanation: As the central bank, the BOT manages currency, monetary policy and the banking system.

summary.questionText: What is the importance of paying taxes to the nation?
summary.correctAnswer: Taxes provide revenue used to fund public services and infrastructure such as schools, hospitals, water and roads.
summary.explanation: Tax revenue enables the government to deliver services and development projects that benefit all citizens.

summary.questionText: Explain why investment is important for economic development.
summary.correctAnswer: Investment creates jobs, increases production, raises incomes, brings in technology and expands government revenue.
summary.explanation: Both local and foreign investment boost output and employment, supporting national development.

summary.questionText: Identify three economic problems facing Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Inflation, unemployment, national debt and economic dependency.
summary.explanation: These challenges slow development and reduce people's standard of living.

summary.questionText: Suggest two ways of solving the problem of unemployment.
summary.correctAnswer: Promoting entrepreneurship and self-employment, encouraging investment that creates jobs, and improving vocational/skills education.
summary.explanation: Creating new businesses, attracting investment and equipping youth with skills help reduce unemployment.

summary.questionText: Explain why managing public resources well is important.
summary.correctAnswer: Good management reduces waste and corruption, ensures resources reach intended services, and promotes fair and sustainable development.
summary.explanation: Proper use of public funds and resources builds trust and enables the government to deliver development for all.

hoq.questionText: A country relies heavily on exporting one cash crop. When the world price of that crop falls sharply, government revenue drops and it struggles to fund services. Which economic problem does this best illustrate?

options.text: Economic dependency on a single product
An increase in the money supply
A balanced national budget
Successful diversification of the economy

hoq.explanation: Depending on one crop or product makes an economy vulnerable to price changes; diversifying production reduces this risk.

hoq.questionText: The government wants to reduce a large budget deficit without cutting essential services. Which combination of measures is most appropriate and sustainable?

options.text: Print more money to cover the gap
Widen the tax base, reduce wasteful spending and fight tax evasion
Borrow heavily from abroad every year
Stop collecting all indirect taxes

hoq.explanation: Increasing revenue through a wider tax base and curbing waste and evasion is more sustainable than printing money or piling up debt, which can cause inflation or a debt burden.

hoq.questionText: A foreign company opens a large factory in Tanzania, hiring local workers and buying local raw materials, but it sends most of its profits back to its home country. Which statement gives the most balanced analysis of this foreign investment?

options.text: It has only benefits and no drawbacks for Tanzania
It is entirely harmful and should be banned
It brings jobs, skills and markets, but profit repatriation reduces the gains kept in the country
It has no effect on the national economy at all

hoq.explanation: Foreign investment creates jobs, transfers skills and creates markets for local materials, but sending profits abroad limits how much benefit remains in the national economy, so policies should encourage reinvestment.
